title: [CQ-I06b] Shared client verdict corpus
description:
Objective: CQ-I06 DoD 1, 'Both clients consume identical daemon verdicts'. Build ONE client-neutral corpus of daemon approval-frame sequences and managed-VM producer reports, and run it through BOTH IDEs' real decision code, so JetBrains and VS Code cannot drift apart. Today each client mirrors the other through its own hand-written tables: I02 against I04, and I03 against I05.

Deliverable:
- NEW moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json. It is a test resource: the plugin jar ships only main resources, and the VS Code vsix never includes moe-jetbrains.
- NEW moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/ClientVerdictCorpusTest.kt, which loads the corpus from the classpath.
- A corpus section in moe-vscode/tests/plan-review.test.cjs that drives the approval rows through the existing real PlanReviewPanel + media/planReview.js harness.
- NEW moe-vscode/tests/managed-vm-verdicts.test.cjs, which drives the VM rows through CQ-I05's src/util/ManagedVm.ts.
Both VS Code files read the same JSON bytes, at ../../moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json.

Out of scope:
- packaging (CQ-I06c), CI and docs (CQ-I06), and the daemon;
- production changes, except a fix-forward for a row the two clients disagree on. Such a fix is at most 20 lines, goes in the owning client module, and is reported in modifiedFiles. Anything bigger becomes a new defect task, and this task calls report_blocked on it.

Verification (run fresh, exit 0 required): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile && cd ../moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test
definitionOfDone: client-verdicts.json holds the plan's approval rows and VM rows, each with exactly one client-neutral expectation. An approval row gives the rendered revision, the ordered daemon events, and one verdict: confirmed, rearmed, latched or pending. A VM row gives the command, stdout, exit and timedOut, plus its verdict, readiness and actions. No row is client-specific.

ClientVerdictCorpusTest runs every approval row through MoeJson.parseTask + PlanReviewApprovalState, and every VM row through ManagedVmPresentation. It asserts each row's verdict by id, and fails on an empty corpus or an unknown verdict.

The VS Code tests run the SAME bytes: approval rows through the real PlanReviewPanel + planReview.js harness, VM rows through ManagedVm. Each mutant named in the plan fails its row in the client it mutates.
Fresh `cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile && cd ../moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` exits 0 for both clients, and the output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: One corpus, two consumers: never give one client a different expectation, skip, or tolerance for a row; a disagreement is fixed or filed, never encoded.
